questions.prompt: A *thematic map* shows:
choices: How one theme, such as tree height, varies from place to place
Every feature in an area, in the same color
A photo taken from the air
questions.explain: Thematic maps focus on one variable, such as income or building age, across space.

questions.prompt: In an sf object, each row is one:
questions.explain: Each row is a feature (a tree, a building), and each column is an attribute.

questions.prompt: What makes an sf object different from an ordinary data frame?
choices: A geometry column holding each feature's point, line, or polygon
It can't be used with dplyr
questions.explain: Apart from the geometry column, it is an ordinary data frame, so tidyverse verbs still work.

questions.prompt: Which function reads a GeoJSON file into an sf object?
questions.explain: `read_sf("Tree_Inventory.geojson")` returns an sf object.

questions.prompt: Complete the code to map the trees as dots.
questions.explain: `tm_shape()` names the data; the layer function after it draws it.

questions.prompt: Which layer function draws a sidewalk network?
questions.explain: `tm_lines()` draws line features.

questions.prompt: Which layer function draws building footprints with a fill and an outline?
questions.explain: Polygons have an inside, so `tm_polygons()` fills them.

questions.prompt: Which is the right way to color trees by height in tmap?
questions.explain: tmap takes column names as text, in quotes, unlike ggplot2's `aes()`.

questions.prompt: To color lines by a column, tmap uses `col =` rather than `fill =`.
questions.explain: A line has no inside to fill, so its color is set with `col`.

questions.prompt: `HEIGHT` is a numeric column. What kind of palette does tmap use for it by default?
choices: Qualitative: distinct colors with no order
questions.explain: Numbers get a sequential palette so bigger values look darker.

questions.prompt: `COMMONNAME` is a text column. What kind of palette does tmap use?
choices: Qualitative: one distinct color per category
Diverging: two colors meeting in the middle
questions.explain: Categories have no order, so they get distinct colors.

questions.prompt: With 158 tree species, the map is unreadable. Which is a good fix?
choices: Keep the most common species and label the rest "other"
questions.explain: `mutate()` with `if_else()` lumps rare categories together, so every tree stays on the map.

questions.prompt: In `if_else(COMMONNAME %in% top_nine, COMMONNAME, "other")`, what happens to a tree whose `COMMONNAME` is `NA`?
choices: It is removed from the data
questions.explain: `NA %in% top_nine` is `FALSE`, so the tree gets "other".

questions.prompt: Why use `st_drop_geometry()` before `count(COMMONNAME)`?
choices: It makes counting much faster, because sf won't merge the points of each species
questions.explain: Without it, sf tries to combine all the points of each group into one shape.

questions.prompt: A map of buildings shaded by year built is a:
questions.explain: A choropleth shades areas by a value.

questions.prompt: In `tm_scale_intervals(n = 4, style = "equal")`, what does `n` set?
questions.explain: `n` is how many classes; `style` is how the breaks are chosen.

questions.prompt: With `style = "equal"`, the classes:
choices: Each cover the same range of values
Each hold the same number of features
Break where the gaps in the data are largest
questions.explain: Equal intervals split the range evenly. `"quantile"` puts the same number of features in each class, and `"jenks"` uses the gaps.

questions.prompt: Complete the tmap v4 code for four equal-interval classes.
questions.explain: In tmap v4, classification goes in `fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals()`.

questions.prompt: You add `map_buildings + map_sidewalks + map_trees`. Why do the buildings go first?
choices: They set the map extent, and later layers draw on top of them
questions.explain: Layers draw in order, and the first sets the extent. Polygons first, points last, so nothing gets covered.

questions.prompt: Which function adds a north arrow?
questions.explain: `tm_compass()` adds the north arrow; `tm_scalebar()` adds the scale bar.

questions.prompt: What does `tmap_mode("view")` do?
choices: Makes interactive web maps you can pan and zoom
Saves the map as a PNG
questions.explain: View mode puts the map on a basemap in a web map. `tmap_mode("plot")` switches back to static maps.

questions.prompt: View mode needs an internet connection to load its basemap tiles.
questions.explain: The basemap tiles come from the web.

questions.prompt: In `tm_bubbles(size = "pop2030", fill = "orange")`, which argument is *mapped* to the data?
questions.explain: `"pop2030"` is a column, so size comes from the data. `"orange"` is a fixed color, so every bubble is orange.

questions.prompt: Put the pieces in order to map the buildings by number of floors.
questions.explain: Pipe the data into `tm_shape()`, then add the layer with `+`.
